name: Hypothesis
why_listed: Classes and research groups who want to annotate the same web page, PDF or YouTube transcript together and discuss in threads would use Hypothesis instead of Spoken Margins' shared Margins.

platforms.value: web: Chrome/Chromium extension, bookmarklet for other browsers, LMS apps (Canvas, Blackboard, Moodle, D2L); no native mobile app
platforms.detail: Browser-based annotation layer; on phones only via an unofficial bookmarklet workaround.

sources.title: How to Use Hypothesis on Mobile Devices : Hypothesis
sources.quote: Currently, Hypothesis officially provides a Chrome extension and a bookmarklet. Most major browsers, however, only support extensions or bookmarklets on desktop computers and laptops.

sources.title: Hypothesis | The #1 Social Annotation Tool for Higher Education
sources.quote: all without leaving Canvas, Blackboard, Moodle, or D2L.

price_free_tier.value: Free: core annotation and private groups (free account)
price_free_tier.detail: Individuals annotate for free; paid packages are for institutions' LMS use.

plays_podcasts.detail: Annotation layer for text, PDFs, videos and images; does not subscribe to or play podcasts.

sources.quote: Hypothesis works seamlessly across every content type your students encounter:

plays_podcasts.note: The homepage section 'What Can Be Annotated with Hypothesis?' (webpages, online PDFs, videos, images, eTexts, online articles) is treated as the comprehensive list of what it works on.

reads_web_articles_aloud.detail: No text-to-speech; it annotates pages the browser displays.

sources.title: Hypothesis | The #1 Social Annotation Tool for Higher Education
sources.quote: Annotate articles, research, and course readings right where you find them—directly in your browser.

reads_web_articles_aloud.note: The homepage section 'What Can Be Annotated with Hypothesis?' (webpages, online PDFs, videos, images, eTexts, online articles) is treated as the comprehensive list of what it works on.

sources.title: Hypothesis | The #1 Social Annotation Tool for Higher Education
sources.quote: Highlight and annotate papers, readings, and handouts directly in the document.

reads_pdfs_aloud.note: The homepage section 'What Can Be Annotated with Hypothesis?' (webpages, online PDFs, videos, images, eTexts, online articles) is treated as the comprehensive list of what it works on.

voice_notes_anchored.detail: Annotations are text with formatting, links, images, LaTeX and embedded YouTube videos; no voice recording.

sources.title: Annotation Basics : Hypothesis
sources.quote: When creating an annotation, use the toolbar above your note to format text, and add links, pictures, or equations (in LaTeX format) .

voice_notes_anchored.note: The Annotation Basics page describes the full annotation editor; no audio recording is mentioned.

text_notes_anchored.detail: Typed annotations on selected text in web pages and PDFs, and on YouTube transcript lines that jump to that point in the video.

sources.title: Annotation Basics : Hypothesis
sources.quote: Log in to Hypothesis and use your cursor to select any text.

sources.title: Annotating YouTube Videos With the Hypothesis Web App : Hypothesis
sources.quote: You can select text anywhere in the transcript to create a new annotation or highlight.

hands_free_capture.detail: Annotation is done by selecting text in a desktop browser.

sources.quote: Log in to Hypothesis and use your cursor to select any text.

hands_free_capture.note: The homepage section 'What Can Be Annotated with Hypothesis?' (webpages, online PDFs, videos, images, eTexts, online articles) is treated as the comprehensive list of what it works on.

transcripts.detail: Shows YouTube transcripts beside the video for annotation (video must have a transcript); no podcasts.

sources.title: Annotating YouTube Videos With the Hypothesis Web App : Hypothesis
sources.quote: you will see the YouTube video, the transcript, and the Hypothesis sidebar all in one window.

ai_summaries.detail: No AI summary feature found; the vendor positions the product against AI summarising.

sources.title: Hypothesis | The #1 Social Annotation Tool for Higher Education
sources.quote: real learning happens when students engage directly with ideas — not when they summarize them for an AI.

ai_summaries.note: Checked homepage, pricing page and the help articles above; no AI summary or chapter feature is mentioned, but the help centre was not searched exhaustively.

export_markdown_pkm.detail: Exports annotations as JSON, plain text, CSV or HTML; no Markdown or Obsidian/Notion/Readwise integration from the vendor.

sources.title: Exporting and Importing Annotations : Hypothesis
sources.quote: You may choose from JSON, plain text, CSV, and HTML exports.

export_markdown_pkm.note: Third-party tools exist but were not counted.

share_note_at_moment.detail: Each annotation has its own link that opens it in context on the source page; works for text, PDFs and YouTube transcripts.

sources.title: Annotation Basics : Hypothesis
sources.quote: Every annotation has various components, including a unique link (aka URL) you can use to share it on social media, via email, or by copying the link to paste elsewhere.

sources.title: Annotation Basics : Hypothesis
sources.quote: links to visit the original source and annotations in context

share_note_at_moment.note: Requires the recipient to open it in a browser with Hypothesis; not an audio moment.

group_listening.detail: Public layer and private groups with threaded replies and mentions; built for classes.

sources.title: Annotation Basics : Hypothesis
sources.quote: Use the groups menu in the sidebar to choose whether to post your finished note in the public layer or in one of your groups.

sources.title: Hypothesis | The #1 Social Annotation Tool for Higher Education
sources.quote: Students, faculty, and teams can share ideas, ask questions, provide insights and respond directly to annotations.

on_device_privacy.detail: Annotations are stored in the Hypothesis service under an account; private ones are 'Only Me' on the server.

sources.title: Annotation Basics : Hypothesis
sources.quote: You’ll need to log in to create annotations and to see private or group annotations.

account_required.detail: Viewing public annotations works without logging in; creating annotations requires a free account (or LMS login).

sources.title: Annotation Basics : Hypothesis
